items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: Gerry would say... it might have been him and Coleman Hawkins and Ben Webster and whoever, then it’s more of what we’re talking about as a democratic process of those guys are playing together

ctx.x: I am but I’m also quoting from a review on your Gerry Mulligan book and it said for one Mulligan took the managerial aspect of being a bandleader seriously. His approach pours cold water on the romantic ideal that a jazz band is about unfettered democracy.

I could very much speak to that from personal experience in many of these things. It truly is a case by case, band by band kind of a thing. There has to be a leader. Gerry was always very specific and he’s absolutely a thousand percent right, there has to be a leader. So it’s a democratic process when they are actually playing together, because then that role isn’t required. I mean you know then it’s a process where they’re creating music together and everyone has a role that they can take liberties with as…

interpretations. But even for what I do, and I learned very early on of having to put different bands together and create different things. You can’t just usually put a band together and hope that — and say, “Okay we want you to play — we want you to do a tribute to Jazz at the Philharmonic and we want you to do a Jazz at the Philharmonic type concert” because there’ll be a lot of standing around and either one of two things will happen. Either one person that’s a Gerry Mulligan type will just step forward and…
